Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National | Top Story Presidency orders state CEOs who have reached retirement limits to vacate office Source : Myjoyonline.com 23 November 2026 9:23pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Chief Executives of public institutions and state-owned organisations who have exceeded the constitutional retirement limits have been directed to hand over and vacate office, following a new instruction from the Office of the President.
The directive requires all Ministers of State to ensure that CEOs under their respective oversight comply with Article 199 of the 1992 Constitution, which sets the compulsory retirement age for public officers at 60, subject to specified exceptions and re-engagement arrangements.
In a letter dated November 23, 2026, and signed by the Secretary to the President, Dr Callistus Mahama, ministers were instructed to ensure that affected chief executives submit their handing-over notes to their respective Boards or Councils without delay.
The instruction applies to CEOs who have attained the age of 60 but are serving without a valid post-retirement contract, as well as those whose contracts have expired or who have exhausted the maximum period permitted for re-engagement.
The Presidency cited Article 199(4), which allows an appointing authority to re-engage a retired public officer where the needs of the service require it.
Under the provision, such engagements may be granted for periods of up to two years at a time, but must not exceed five years cumulatively.
The letter explained that where re-engagement begins at age 60, the maximum period would end at age 65.
It therefore directed that chief executives who have reached the applicable limits should complete the handover process and leave office. Those approaching the end of their lawful tenure must submit their handing-over notes by their final day in office.
The handing-over notes are expected to outline ongoing programmes, outstanding decisions and commitments, and issues requiring the immediate attention of the relevant Board or Council.
The directive places responsibility on ministers to ensure that institutions under their supervision comply with the constitutional requirements.
